The seventh edition of West Africa Mining Activities Week (SAMAO) will be held from 25 to 27 September 2025 in Ouagadougou. The broad outlines of this major event were presented on Tuesday, 16 September 2025.

From 25 to 27 September 2025, Ouagadougou will vibrate to the rhythm of West Africa Mining Activities Week. During these 72 hours, the various activities will revolve around the theme "The challenges of rehabilitating and closing mines in Africa: what new life for local communities?"

According to Doulaye Sanou, president of the organising committee, this edition will constitute a framework for exchanging experiences between public and private actors from various countries for the sustainable management of mineral resources. "It will serve as a platform for mining industry actors to discuss the issue of the rehabilitation and closure of mines, with the future of local communities as the backdrop," he specified.

He further indicated that at least 2,000 participants from Burkina Faso, the sub-region and the rest of the world are expected at SAMAO, which will be held at the Ouaga 2000 International Conference Centre. Doulaye Sanou added that a session will be devoted to presenting innovations for more environmentally friendly mining. He also reported that the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) will be honoured through a session dedicated to presenting their achievements in relation to mine rehabilitation. The programme also includes technical workshops, B2B meetings, exhibitions of mining equipment, and visits to mining sites and quarries.

In parallel with SAMAO, other activities, dubbed "pre-SAMAO activities," will be held on the theme: "Developing an environmentally friendly cement industry from Burkina Faso's local resources: between technical challenges and economic opportunities."

Accordingly, Doulaye Sanou explained that this workshop aims to contribute to the development of local materials in Burkina Faso's cement industry. "It will thus make it possible, among other things, to make known the existing potential of quarry substances that can be used in cement manufacturing and to explore the economic and industrial opportunities linked to the exploitation of local resources in order to reduce dependence on imports and strengthen the capacity of national industries," he maintained.

Aminata Catherine SANOU

Cet accord ambitionne de déboucher à terme sur « une fin définitive de la guerre », lors de plusieurs phases définies par Israël et le Hamas.
GAZA - Une première phase concrète, avant le saut dans l’inconnu. Avec l’annonce retardée du feu vert israélien, le cessez-le-feu entre l’État hébreu et le Hamas entrera en vigueur ce dimanche 19 janvier à 7h30 (heure française), mettant fin à quinze moins de conflit dans l’enclave palestinienne dévastée par la guerre.
Fruit de longues et âpres négociations entre les deux parties, encadrées par des pays médiateurs, la trêve doit notamment permettre de libérer les otages israéliens encore retenus dans la bande de Gaza, tout en mettant provisoirement fin au conflit armé qui a fait des dizaines de milliers de morts depuis l’attaque du Hamas en territoire israélien, le 7 octobre 2023.
Le cessez-le-feu devra respecter plusieurs phases - trois - selon les détails fournis par le Qatar et les États-Unis, principaux pays à la manœuvre pour aboutir à cette interruption de la guerre.
· Première journée cruciale
Actée pour ce dimanche, la trêve doit déboucher dès son premier jour sur la libération de premiers otages israéliens. En contrepartie, Israël s’est engagé à relâcher des prisonniers palestiniens. Un échange relativement proche, dans sa forme, à celui effectué en novembre 2023 lors de la précédente trêve négociée entre Israël et le Hamas.
La trêve commencera à 8h30, heure locale à Gaza. Mais il faudra sans doute attendre plusieurs heures avant de voir les premiers otages retrouver leur liberté, après 470 jours de captivité à Gaza. Selon deux sources proches du Hamas citées par l’AFP, le premier groupe devrait être composé de trois Israéliennes, mais l’heure de leur libération n’est pas encore connue.
De leur côté, les autorités israéliennes ont désigné 95 détenus libérables ce dimanche. D’ailleurs, Israël a prévu des mesures pour « prévenir toute manifestation publique de joie » à leur sortie et le ministère israélien de la Justice a précisé que la libération de ces premiers prisonniers n’interviendrait pas avant 15h (heure française).
· Une première phase de six semaines
La libération des otages doit s’effectuer par trois points d’accueil mis en place sur la frontière avec Gaza, d’où les otages, pris en charge par des médecins, seront conduits vers des hôpitaux. Selon l’accord, 33 otages israéliens doivent être relâchés. Dans ce groupe, se trouvent notamment les deux otages franco-israéliens Ofer Kalderon et Ohad Yahalomi.
Du côté des prisonniers palestiniens, 737 seront libérés. Parmi eux, se trouvent 70 femmes, dont une mineure, et 25 hommes (dont neuf âgés de moins de 18 ans). Sur cette liste, sept prisonniers seulement ont été arrêtés avant le 7 octobre 2023.
Pour le reste, la première étape sera dédiée à un cessez-le-feu total, ainsi qu’au retrait israélien des zones densément peuplées et à une augmentation de l’aide humanitaire. Dernier point majeur : l’entame de négociations sur les modalités de la deuxième phase, à savoir « une fin définitive de la guerre », comme l’a expliqué le Premier ministre du Qatar, Mohammed ben Abdelrahmane Al-Thani. Dès vendredi, plusieurs pays médiateurs ont convenu de mettre en place une salle d’opération conjointe au Caire en Égypte pour « assurer une coordination efficace » et le respect des conditions de la trêve. Ce qui doit aussi permettre de faciliter l’entrée de 600 camions d’aide par jour.
· Une deuxième étape pour la « fin définitive de la guerre »
Une fois les six premières semaines écoulées, ce qui devrait être le cas autour du 5 mars, la deuxième phase devrait permettre la libération des derniers otages encore captifs dans l’enclave palestinienne.
Pour le reste, « les détails concernant les phases deux et trois seront finalisés lors de la mise en œuvre de la première phase », a déclaré le Premier ministre qatari. « Au cours des six prochaines semaines, Israël négociera les arrangements nécessaires pour passer à la phase deux, qui marquera la fin définitive de la guerre. Je le répète, une fin définitive de la guerre », a poursuivi le président américain Joe Biden.
« Lorsque la phase deux commencera, il y aura un échange pour la libération des otages restants encore vivants, y compris les soldats hommes, et toutes les forces israéliennes restantes se retireront de Gaza. Le cessez-le-feu temporaire deviendra alors permanent », a également indiqué Joe Biden, peu de temps avant de passer la main à Donald Trump.
· Une ultime phase presque entièrement dédiée à Gaza
La troisième et dernière phase du plan de cessez-le-feu prévoit la restitution des corps des otages morts en captivité à Gaza. Selon les estimations de l’armée israélienne, 94 personnes sont encore détenues dans l’enclave depuis le 7 octobre. Et si 33 doivent être libérés, 34 otages ont déjà été déclarés morts par Israël.
Enfin, cette dernière étape du processus sera presque intégralement consacrée à la reconstruction de Gaza.
Source: https://www.huffingtonpost.fr/

This agreement aims eventually to lead to “a definitive end to the war,” through several phases defined by Israel and Hamas.

GAZA – A first concrete phase, before the leap into the unknown. With the delayed announcement of the Israeli green light, the ceasefire between the Hebrew state and Hamas will take effect this Sunday, 19 January, at 7:30 a.m. (French time), ending fifteen months of conflict in the Palestinian enclave devastated by war.

The product of long and bitter negotiations between the two parties, overseen by mediating countries, the truce should notably allow the release of the Israeli hostages still held in the Gaza Strip, while temporarily ending the armed conflict that has killed tens of thousands since the Hamas attack on Israeli territory on 7 October 2023.

The ceasefire is to proceed in several phases – three – according to details provided by Qatar and the United States, the main countries working to bring about this interruption of the war.

· A crucial first day

Set for this Sunday, the truce is to lead on its very first day to the release of the first Israeli hostages. In exchange, Israel has committed to freeing Palestinian prisoners. The exchange is relatively similar in form to the one carried out in November 2023 during the previous truce negotiated between Israel and Hamas.

The truce will begin at 8:30 a.m., local time in Gaza. But it will no doubt take several hours before the first hostages regain their freedom, after 470 days of captivity in Gaza. According to two sources close to Hamas cited by AFP, the first group should be made up of three Israeli women, but the time of their release is not yet known.

For their part, the Israeli authorities have designated 95 detainees eligible for release this Sunday. Israel has also planned measures to “prevent any public display of joy” on their release, and the Israeli Justice Ministry specified that the release of these first prisoners would not take place before 3 p.m. (French time).

· A first phase of six weeks

The release of the hostages is to take place through three reception points set up on the border with Gaza, from which the hostages, taken in hand by doctors, will be driven to hospitals. Under the agreement, 33 Israeli hostages are to be released. Among this group are the two Franco-Israeli hostages Ofer Kalderon and Ohad Yahalomi.

On the Palestinian prisoners’ side, 737 will be freed. Among them are 70 women, including one minor, and 25 men (nine of them under 18). On this list, only seven prisoners were arrested before 7 October 2023.

For the rest, the first stage will be dedicated to a total ceasefire, as well as to an Israeli withdrawal from densely populated areas and an increase in humanitarian aid. A final major point: the opening of negotiations on the terms of the second phase, namely “a definitive end to the war,” as the Prime Minister of Qatar, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, explained. As early as Friday, several mediating countries agreed to set up a joint operations room in Cairo, Egypt, to “ensure effective coordination” and compliance with the terms of the truce. This should also make it possible to facilitate the entry of 600 aid trucks per day.

· A second stage for the “definitive end to the war”

Once the first six weeks have elapsed, which should be around 5 March, the second phase should allow the release of the last hostages still held captive in the Palestinian enclave.

For the rest, “the details concerning phases two and three will be finalised during the implementation of the first phase,” the Qatari Prime Minister said. “Over the next six weeks, Israel will negotiate the necessary arrangements to move to phase two, which will mark the definitive end of the war. I repeat, a definitive end to the war,” US President Joe Biden went on.

“When phase two begins, there will be an exchange for the release of the remaining hostages still alive, including male soldiers, and all remaining Israeli forces will withdraw from Gaza. The temporary ceasefire will then become permanent,” Joe Biden also stated, shortly before handing over to Donald Trump.

· A final phase almost entirely devoted to Gaza

The third and last phase of the ceasefire plan provides for the return of the bodies of hostages who died in captivity in Gaza. According to Israeli army estimates, 94 people are still held in the enclave since 7 October. And while 33 are to be released, 34 hostages have already been declared dead by Israel.

Finally, this last stage of the process will be almost entirely devoted to the reconstruction of Gaza.

Source: https://www.huffingtonpost.fr/

Le Bénin fait un choix révolutionnaire sur le plan sanitaire au profit de ses citoyens. C’est l’intérêt de la Politique nationale de la santé communautaire (Pnsc) dont l’atelier de plaidoyer pour l’accélération de sa mise en œuvre a été lancé, jeudi 20 juillet dernier, au profit des autorités communales et préfectorales.
« Les programmes de santé communautaire sont indispensables pour progresser vers la couverture sanitaire universelle des soins de santé et atteindre les Odd », soutient Carl Anderson, représentant résident de l’Usaid.
Basée sur l’approche « One health », la Pnsc encourage une vision globale de proximité de la santé. Elle contribuera à modifier de manière sensible l’approche béninoise « dans l’offre des soins et services de santé aux populations tout en mettant l’accent sur la prévention et la promotion de la santé, la mise en place d’un dispositif d’alerte pour la survenue des maladies en milieu communautaire. Elle est la traduction d’une véritable révolution sanitaire qui impactera à coup sûr la couverture sanitaire universelle et ce, à moindre coût », se réjouit Benjamin Hounkpatin, ministre de la Santé. 
Ce dispositif sanitaire est un tout. Il implique l’adhésion des acteurs communaux. « La Pnsc engage les élus communaux et les acteurs locaux dans la mise en œuvre de l’accès des populations aux soins préventifs, promotionnels et curatifs, à la veille sanitaire et pour la surveillance épidémiologique des cas de maladies », apprécie-t-il.
Mieux, la Pnsc promeut un capital humain sain, compétent et compétitif, et soutient la mise en place des mécanismes pérennes et inclusifs. Le ministère des Affaires sociales y trouve son compte.  « L’opérationnalisation des relais communautaires est un levier sur lequel le ministère des Affaires sociales pourra prendre action pour faciliter la réussite du programme de filet de protection sociale productif, ‘’Gbésoké’’ ; du projet de l’employabilité des personnes handicapées ; de l’Assurance pour le renforcement du capital humain (Arch) dans son volet assurance maladie, et du Micro crédit Alafia », apprécie Véronique 
Tognifodé, ministre des Affaires sociales et de la Microfinance. 
Pour l’Unicef, l’atelier de plaidoyer était très attendu, car il ouvre une nouvelle page en faveur de la santé communautaire. « Ces assises sont cruciales pour l’Unicef et l’ensemble des partenaires, et montrent le fort engagement et le leadership du gouvernement du Bénin pour renforcer le système de santé communautaire et les soins de santé primaires », souligne Djanabou Mahondé, représentante résidente de l’Unicef.
Le concours de tous
La Pnsc sera concluante si tous les acteurs concernés mettaient la main à la pâte. « Le succès du déploiement de cette nouvelle politique de santé communautaire dépend de l’appropriation et l’implication active des autorités locales à toutes les étapes de sa mise en œuvre », indique Benjamin Hounkpatin.
Le ministère de la Santé est d’ores et déjà prêt à consentir le sacrifice nécessaire en vue d’engranger de réels succès. « Nos équipes et nous-mêmes devrons être constamment engagés dans toutes les étapes de déploiement de la Politique nationale de la santé communautaire dans nos départements et communes, particulièrement lors de la phase d’identification des relais communautaires, du dénombrement des ménages, du suivi des activités des relais communautaires et des agents de santé communautaire qualifiés dans nos villages et dans les arrondissements », souhaite-t-il. 
Le ministre de la Décentralisation et de la Gouvernance locale est au premier rang pour faire bouger les lignes. « Assurant le lead du suivi de la santé communautaire au niveau des départements et des communes, je prends personnellement l’engagement de donner le meilleur de moi-même pour la coordination de toutes les actions de mon secteur entrant dans ce cadre », promet Raphaël Akotègnon. 
La phase pilote de la Politique nationale de la santé communautaire est déjà une réalité dans les communes de Banikoara, 
Bembérèkè, Kalalé, Malanville, Nikki et Sinendé, grâce à l’appui de l’Unicef. Outre l’Unicef, l’Usaid, la Banque mondiale, la Banque islamique de Développement et le Fonds mondial et autres soutiennent ce projet.

Benin is making a revolutionary choice on the health front for the benefit of its citizens. That is the point of the National Community Health Policy (Pnsc), whose advocacy workshop for accelerating its implementation was launched on Thursday 20 July, for the benefit of communal and prefectural authorities.

"Community health programmes are indispensable for making progress towards universal health coverage and achieving the SDGs," maintains Carl Anderson, resident representative of USAID.

Based on the "One Health" approach, the Pnsc encourages a comprehensive, community-level vision of health. It will help to change appreciably the Beninese approach "to the provision of care and health services to the population, while placing the emphasis on prevention and health promotion and on the establishment of an alert system for the occurrence of diseases in the community setting. It is the expression of a true health revolution which will certainly have an impact on universal health coverage, and at lower cost," rejoices Benjamin Hounkpatin, Minister of Health.

This health arrangement is a whole. It requires the buy-in of communal actors. "The Pnsc commits communal elected officials and local actors to implementing the population's access to preventive, promotional and curative care, to health watch and to the epidemiological surveillance of disease cases," he observes.

Better still, the Pnsc promotes healthy, competent and competitive human capital, and supports the establishment of lasting and inclusive mechanisms. The Ministry of Social Affairs finds its own benefit in it. "Making community relays operational is a lever on which the Ministry of Social Affairs will be able to act in order to facilitate the success of the productive social safety net programme, 'Gbesoke'; the project for the employability of persons with disabilities; the Insurance for the Strengthening of Human Capital (Arch) in its health insurance component; and the Alafia Micro-credit," observes Veronique Tognifode, Minister of Social Affairs and Microfinance.

For UNICEF, the advocacy workshop was much awaited, because it opens a new page in favour of community health. "These proceedings are crucial for UNICEF and for all the partners, and show the strong commitment and leadership of the government of Benin in strengthening the community health system and primary health care," underlines Djanabou Mahonde, resident representative of UNICEF.

Everyone's contribution

The Pnsc will be conclusive if all the actors concerned put their hands to the task. "The success of the rollout of this new community health policy depends on the ownership and active involvement of local authorities at every stage of its implementation," indicates Benjamin Hounkpatin.

The Ministry of Health is already prepared to make the necessary sacrifice in order to secure real successes. "Our teams and we ourselves must be constantly engaged at all stages of the rollout of the National Community Health Policy in our departments and communes, particularly during the phase of identifying community relays, counting households, and monitoring the activities of community relays and of qualified community health workers in our villages and boroughs," he hopes.

The Minister of Decentralisation and Local Governance is in the front rank in shifting the lines. "As the lead for the monitoring of community health at the level of the departments and communes, I personally undertake to give my best for the coordination of all the actions of my sector falling within this framework," promises Raphael Akotegnon.

The pilot phase of the National Community Health Policy is already a reality in the communes of Banikoara, Bemberelke [Bemberekel/Bemberekle], Kalale, Malanville, Nikki and Sinende, thanks to UNICEF's support. Besides UNICEF, USAID, the World Bank, the Islamic Development Bank, the Global Fund and others support this project.

South Africa, Somalia 'kingmakers' as geopolitical strategies play out in Africa
Deteriorating relations between Taiwan and economic powerhouse South Africa and the Federal Republic of Somalia, both of which are fervent backers of the "one-China” principle, have highlighted the surging influence of Beijing in Africa.
It comes at a time when the relationship between Pretoria and Washington has soured due to U.S. President Donald Trump’s imposition of a 30% tariff on South African exports, largely stemming from the republic’s genocide case against American ally Israel at the International Court of Justice.
The U.S. government also slashed USAID-backed projects worth more than $400m in famine-affected Somalia this year, according to documents leaked by Congress and analysed by The Independent news outlet in the UK.
South Africa, a BRICS member, and Somalia have made no secret of their allegiance to China as titanic geopolitical shifts unfold.
Similarly, Xi Jinping’s government has been quick to spot an opportunity to further cement its influence in Africa while furthering its ambitions to bring Taiwan, another U.S. ally, into its fold after decades of tense stand-off.
Both South Africa and Somalia have taken steps against Taiwan in recent months, which, while seemingly slight within the broader global context, sends a clear signal that they stand firmly on the side of China.
Earlier this year, South Africa officially withdrew its recognition of Taiwan’s representative office in the capital of Pretoria – reportedly without even consulting Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
South Africa has been putting pressure on Taiwan to move its office out of the capital to Johannesburg, arguing that having it in the administrative seat of government violates the country’s one-China principle, adopted in 1998.
Yet Pretoria also insists its relationship with Taiwan is "non-political” and any decision made is based on "fundamentally shifting” economic diplomacy.
United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758 was adopted in 1971 to accommodate the People’s Republic of China’s inclusion. It meant that the Republic of China, Taiwan's official name, could no longer be represented.
Taiwan initially did not take South Africa’s pressure to relocate its office lying down.
In September, it rolled out a series of restrictions on the export of advanced semiconductor chips to South Africa – crucial to the republic’s automotive sector, which is already struggling under U.S. tariffs.
Taiwan then backtracked on the move, ostensibly because it would hurt the interests of theTaiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world’s largest chip manufacturer.
The about-turn was also driven by South Africa’s willingness to engage in talks.
Somalia, meanwhile, was even more explicit in its actions against Taiwan, banning all Taiwanese passport-holders from entering the country in April.
This, too, was later lifted due to pressure from the United States.
Taiwan has ramped up efforts to establish strong ties with Somaliland, which broke away from Somalia 34 years ago.
While Somaliland is not recognised by any sovereign state, Taiwan has now established a diplomatic office there and Somaliland one in Taipei. In addition, Taiwan and Somaliland are on the brink of signing an historic military cooperation agreement.
Taiwan has already provided military training to Somaliland’s soldiers.
As these developments occur, China is using its economic might to ensure its two African supporters continue to solidify its position on the continent.
In 2024 alone, China invested $13.21 billion in South Africa, 92% of which was in the form of manufactured goods. Chinese carmakers Chery and GWM also intend assembling vehicles in South Africa, where their brands’ market share is soaring annually.
Last year, China and Somalia also announced a $1.2 billion investment partnership to improve infrastructure, energy and agriculture sectors in the East African nation.
Furthermore, China is significantly bolstering Somalia’s aquaculture industry through financial support and training.
With all that has occurred in the past 24 months, it is apparent that South Africa and Somalia are increasingly being viewed as important strategic points in an intensifying geopolitical battle between China and the U.S.
In a climate of trade uncertainty and blatant power-brokerage, these two nations suddenly find themselves in the once-unlikely position of kingmaker.
Though China currently holds sway, South Africa and Somalia also recognise that they cannot yet afford to completely sever ties with the U.S. or Taiwan.
Doing so would deal a crippling economic blow, particularly to South Africa’s auto sector.
For Somalia, which retains its status as a key U.S. ally in the region despite the travel ban friction with Taiwan, there is still a reliance on American aid, even if it is not what it once was.
The next 12 months will prove decisive in which way the pendulum swings.
Kingmakers they may be, but South Africa and Somalia also will need to perform a fine balancing act if they are to safeguard their own interests.

(Des localités très avancées dans les opérations Pfr)
Du lundi 03 mai au vendredi 07 mai dernier,  une délégation constituée des responsables du Millénium challenge account (Mca) et du ministère de l’urbanisme et de la réforme foncière a parcouru plusieurs localités du Bénin où sont installées des stations permanentes Cors/Gnss ainsi que  celles où se réalisent  les Plans fonciers ruraux.  
Entre autres objectifs, cette tournée vise à faire le point des travaux de réalisation de ces instruments modernes, à sensibiliser les autorités locales sur les intérêts qu’ils génèrent et les rôles qu’elles sont appelées à jouer pour leur bon fonctionnement.
Le lundi 03 mai, cap a été mis dans la matinée sur le village de Méhounta, commune de Lokossa. Là attendaient déjà une foule de populations et des responsables locaux en charge des Plans fonciers ruraux ( Pfr). L’activité prévue ici est la visite de la publicité du Pfr dans ce village suivie des échanges avec les différentes structures locales mises en place dans ce cadre. Plusieurs points on été abordés, à savoir, définition et éléments constitutifs d’un Pfr, son processus d’élaboration et les rôles des stations permanentes, leur utilité, les difficultés et mesures prises ainsi que les perspectives. Les responsables de la délégation ont surtout mis l’accent sur la nécessité de poursuivre les sensibilisations avec beaucoup plus d’ardeur afin d’atteindre les résultats attendus. Reste que le cas de ce village est illustratif de l’intérêt que portent les populations locales aux Pfr car les avancées notées dans leur réalisation sont significatives, suivant plusieurs appréciations.
Après leur installation, les 7 stations permanentes Cors/Gnss reparties dans plusieurs localités du Bénin tournent déjà à plein temps. Le constat a été fait dans la même journée du lundi 03 mai par la délégation composée des représentants du programme du Millénium challenge account pour le Bénin (Mca) et du ministère en charge en charge de l’urbanisme, de la réforme foncière et de la lutte contre l’érosion côtière. Visiter lesdites stations, évaluer leur état de fonctionnement, sensibiliser les autorités locales sur les rôles qu’elles auront à jouer pour une bonne préservation de ces appareils ultra-modernes qu’offrent ainsi les américains au Bénin pour une meilleure sécurisation foncière de ses terres. Ce sont entre autres, les grands objectifs visés. A Abomey, comme à Parakou, tout semble bien aller sur les sites. En dépit de quelques difficultés en fourniture énergétique qui se posent déjà par ces temps de délestage. La satisfaction exprimée par le ministre en charge de l’urbanisme et de la réforme foncière, François Noudégbessi est entière, même s’il craint que d’éventuelles difficultés viennent perturber les installations. Il insistera plusieurs fois sur la fourniture en énergie électrique malgré le groupe électrogène disponible sur les lieux et le maintien de la communication téléphonique à haut débit ; car martèle-t-il, « ces stations ne doivent souffrir d’aucune défaillance ». Des instructions ont été données ici aux autorités locales pour mener au plus tôt les démarches nécessaires auprès de la Sbee, afin de privilégier les lignes qui alimentent ces stations.
Dans d’autres localités parcourues, comme celle de Kandi,  les préoccupations sont les mêmes. «  La station permanente est très importante  car  elle facilitera désormais  la gestion foncière. Nous vous exhortons donc à nous aider à la conserver précieusement » a dit  Dah Dossoumon Apollinaire, Directeur général de l’Ign, membre de cette délégation. Le maire de Kandi, Sanni Gounou,  ne  souhaite pas mieux. Il pense d’ailleurs que ces stations permanentes seront d’une grande importance pour  le règlement définitif des conflits fonciers dans sa commune et mettront fin aux drames qui y sont liés.
 
Les Pfr en bonne marche à Gogounou
A Gogounou, la délégation a pu faire un constat plus ou moins satisfaisant dans les travaux de réalisation des Pfr. Les opérations sont sur la bonne voie ici, à la satisfaction générale des populations et des autorités locales. Mais tout n’est pas encore rose. Ces opérations ont occasionné quelques accrochages entre différents propriétaires de terres. Des cas de décès et des dégâts matériels ont été enregistrés, à en croire un élu local. Les membres de la délégation ont déploré ces malheureux faits et ont exprimé leur souci de voir la paix revenir dans les villages concernés.
La station permanente de Natitingou, comme toutes les précédentes fonctionne déjà aussi. Le représentant du Préfet de l’Atacora-Donga, Kassoumou Nassirou qui a reçu la délégation en visite de courtoisie n’a pas caché sa joie. « Nous remercions le Mca-Bénin et le Mcc pour tout ceux qu’ils font pour nous et tout ce qu’ils feront également pour nous » a-t-il laissé entendre. La station permanente de Savalou a également accueilli la délégation au dernier jour de la tournée. Les constats sont similaires. Tout marche bien, mais des soucis en matière d’énergie électrique, de communication par Internet sont une fois encore revenus. « La mise en service des stations permanentes constitue déjà une grande solution à la sécurisation foncière, leur entretien doit donc être un souci majeur » a insisté, Lucien Babagbéto, du ministère de l’urbanisme. Il indiquera plus tard à la presse, que la question de l’insécurité foncière demeure une grande préoccupation pour le gouvernement du Dr Boni Yayi.
Le Directeur du Projet « Accès au foncier », Séyidou Bio Baguiri pense pour sa part que l’objectif de cette tournée a été atteint, car il se dit heureux que les diverses autorités locales rencontrées ont pu comprendre le bien fondé de ces stations permanentes qui permettront entre autres, d’élaborer des Pfr avec des précisions jamais vues au Bénin. En dotant certaines localités de ces stations permanentes dont le coût estimatif pour chacune est environ 500 millions de Fcfa, les américains positionnent ainsi le Bénin au deuxième rang en Afrique, après l’Afrique du Sud. Un plan d’appropriation desdites stations permettra à l’Ign, de continuer à les gérer convenablement au terme du programme Mca-Bénin après le 05 octobre 2011.

(Localities very far advanced in the RLP operations)

From Monday 3 May to Friday 7 May, a delegation made up of officials of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) and of the Ministry of Urban Planning and Land Reform travelled through several localities of Benin where CORS/GNSS permanent stations are installed, as well as those where the Rural Land Plans (Plans fonciers ruraux, PFR) are being carried out.

Among other objectives, this tour aims to take stock of the work of building these modern instruments, to raise the awareness of local authorities about the benefits they generate and the roles they are called upon to play for their proper functioning.

On Monday 3 May, the delegation headed in the morning for the village of Mehounta, in the commune of Lokossa. There, a crowd of local people and local officials in charge of the Rural Land Plans (PFR) were already waiting. The activity planned here was a visit to the public display of the PFR in this village, followed by discussions with the various local structures set up for this purpose. Several points were addressed, namely the definition and constituent elements of a PFR, its drafting process and the roles of the permanent stations, their usefulness, the difficulties and the measures taken, as well as the prospects. The heads of the delegation placed particular emphasis on the need to pursue awareness-raising with much more energy in order to achieve the expected results. The case of this village is illustrative of the interest local people take in the PFRs, since the progress noted in their implementation is significant, according to several assessments.

After their installation, the 7 CORS/GNSS permanent stations spread across several localities of Benin are already running full time. This was observed on the same day, Monday 3 May, by the delegation made up of representatives of the Millennium Challenge Account programme for Benin (MCA) and of the ministry in charge of urban planning, land reform and the fight against coastal erosion. Visiting the said stations, assessing their operating condition, and raising local authorities' awareness of the roles they will have to play in the proper preservation of these ultra-modern devices which the Americans are thus providing to Benin for better security of land tenure: these are, among others, the main objectives pursued. In Abomey, as in Parakou, everything seems to be going well at the sites, despite some difficulties in the power supply that are already arising in these times of load-shedding. The satisfaction expressed by the minister in charge of urban planning and land reform, Francois Noudegbessi, is complete, even if he fears that possible difficulties may disrupt the installations. He insisted several times on the supply of electricity, despite the generator available on site, and on maintaining high-speed telephone communication; for, as he hammers home, "these stations must not suffer any failure." Instructions were given here to local authorities to take the necessary steps as soon as possible with SBEE, in order to give priority to the lines supplying these stations.

In the other localities visited, such as Kandi, the concerns are the same. "The permanent station is very important because it will from now on facilitate land management. We therefore urge you to help us preserve it carefully," said Dah Dossoumon Apollinaire, Director General of the IGN, a member of this delegation. The mayor of Kandi, Sanni Gounou, wants nothing more. He believes, moreover, that these permanent stations will be of great importance for the definitive settlement of land conflicts in his commune and will put an end to the tragedies linked to them.

The RLPs progressing well in Gogounou

In Gogounou, the delegation was able to make a more or less satisfactory observation of the work on the PFRs. Operations are on the right track here, to the general satisfaction of the population and local authorities. But not everything is rosy yet. These operations have caused some clashes between various landowners. Cases of death and material damage have been recorded, according to a local elected official. The members of the delegation deplored these unfortunate facts and expressed their wish to see peace return to the villages concerned.

The Natitingou permanent station, like all the previous ones, is also already operating. The representative of the Prefect of Atacora-Donga, Kassoumou Nassirou, who received the delegation on a courtesy visit, did not hide his joy. "We thank MCA-Benin and the MCC for all they do for us and all they will also do for us," he said. The Savalou permanent station also welcomed the delegation on the last day of the tour. The observations are similar. Everything is working well, but concerns about electric power and internet communication came up once again. "The commissioning of the permanent stations already constitutes a great solution for land tenure security; their maintenance must therefore be a major concern," insisted Lucien Babagbeto, of the Ministry of Urban Planning. He would later tell the press that the question of land insecurity remains a major preoccupation for the government of Dr Boni Yayi.

The Director of the "Access to Land" Project, Seyidou Bio Baguiri, for his part, believes that the objective of this tour has been achieved, as he says he is happy that the various local authorities met were able to understand the merits of these permanent stations, which will make it possible, among other things, to draw up PFRs with a precision never before seen in Benin. By equipping certain localities with these permanent stations, each costing an estimated 500 million CFA francs, the Americans are thus placing Benin second in Africa, after South Africa. An ownership plan for the said stations will allow the IGN to continue managing them properly at the end of the MCA-Benin programme after 5 October 2011.

a4224.t:
US Agency for International Development staff around the world will be placed on administrative leave Friday and ordered to return to the US, according to a directive issued Tuesday night.
As of 11:59 p.m. ET Friday, “all USAID direct hire personnel will be placed on administrative leave globally, with the exception of designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs,” said a statement posted on the USAID website, which is back online after going dark last week.
The statement said it is preparing a plan for personnel posted outside the United States “under which the Agency would arrange and pay for return travel to the United States within 30 days” and terminate “contracts that are not determined to be essential.”
People demonstrate outside of the headquarters for United States Agency for International Development before Congressional Democrats hold news conference in Washington, DC, on February 3.
As the name implies, a direct hire is a government official directly employed by the US government, as opposed to contractors, who make up a large part of the USAID workforce. Many of those contractors have already been furloughed or laid off. Essential personnel expected to continue working will be informed by Thursday afternoon.
The statement on the website ends with: “Thank you for your service.”
The directive comes as the Trump administration has begun dismantling the agency and frozen almost all foreign aid as it signals it plans to fully abolish it as an independent agency.
It is not legal for the president to unilaterally “abolish, move, or consolidate USAID,” a report this week from the Congressional Research Service affirmed. He needs to have congressional authorization to do so.
On Monday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced he would be acting administrator of USAID, confirming the de-facto takeover of the humanitarian agency by the State Department.
In recent days, dozens of senior USAID officials have been placed on leave, thousands of contractors have been laid off, and employees were told this week not to report to the agency’s Washington headquarters.
CNN reported earlier that staffers were receiving individual emails Tuesday informing them that they were being put on leave. Multiple officials shared with CNN the notice from the acting deputy administrator, Peter Marocco.
“You will remain on administrative leave with pay until otherwise notified,” the notice states.
“During the period that you are on administrative leave you are not to enter USAID premises, access USAID systems, or attempt to use your position or authority with USAID in any way without my prior permission or prior permission of a supervisor in your chain of command,” Marocco says in the letter.
A rural groundwater borehole water supply in Turkana, Kenya, funded in part by USAID and supported by the Mortenson Center at the University of Colorado Boulder.
When a reporter told President Donald Trump on Tuesday that it sounded like he was going to “wind down” the agency, he laughed and said, “Sounds like it.”
“Look at all the fraud that he’s found in this USAID,” the president said of Elon Musk, the tech billionaire leading the Department of Governmental Efficiency. “It has to be corrupt,” Trump added without evidence.
Marocco’s Tuesday letter instructed employees to email a USAID official with their “personal contact information, including your phone number, email and mailing address,” so they can remain available during regular business hours. A USAID employee told CNN they emailed and got a bounceback, saying that person is also on leave.
“People are hysterical. My friends are crying. We don’t know what’s going on,” said one USAID official put on leave. They noted that officials posted abroad may have children in school or spouses with jobs, and now that is “all uprooted.”
“No access to any government system; can’t see emails. It’s like we’re criminals,” the official said.
On Monday, thousands of personal services contractors and civil servants lost access to email and USAID systems overnight. The sudden chaos has left employees struggling to get any answers, officials said.
Additionally, USAID headquarters and annex offices in the Washington, DC, area will remain closed the remainder of the week, according to an email sent to staff Tuesday and obtained by CNN. The offices closed include the headquarters in Washington; a second DC annex location; an office in Leesburg, Virginia; and one in Springfield, Virginia.
People protest outside of the headquarters for United States Agency for International Development before Congressional Democrats hold news conference in Washington, DC, on February 3.
“Agency personnel normally assigned to work at these USAID properties should telework this week,” the email said.
There are some exceptions for personnel with essential on-site and building maintenance functions, the email said. The email noted employees are still “expected to remain available during regular business hours and operations.”
Shortly after being sworn in last month, Trump issued a sweeping executive order pausing all foreign aid for 90 days, leading to widespread confusion, layoffs and program shutdowns.
USAID was established in 1961 under President John F. Kennedy’s administration and is the US government’s humanitarian arm. It dispenses billions of dollars annually across the world in an effort to alleviate poverty, treat diseases, and respond to famines and natural disasters.
Musk has led the Trump administration’s effort to weaken USAID, falsely calling it a “viper’s nest of radical-left marxists who hate America” and branding it a “criminal organization” that should “die.”
The Trump administration’s actions have raised questions from Democrats over the legality of any wind-down of the agency that will likely have a dramatic consequence for global life-saving aid from the United States. And a new report from the Congressional Research Service affirmed it is not legal for the president to unilaterally abolish USAID.
“Because Congress established USAID as an independent establishment (defined in 5 U.S.C. 104) within the executive branch, the President does not have the authority to abolish it; congressional authorization would be required to abolish, move, or consolidate USAID,” Monday’s report said.

Pour un management bien outillé de sa gestion, l’Institut national géographique (IGN) a organisé hier, mercredi 8 juillet à Cotonou, une Journée de validation de trois documents stratégiques. Le ministre en charge de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de l’Assainissement, Noël Fonton, a procédé à l’ouverture des travaux.
S’inscrivant dans la logique d’une gestion d’entreprise bien gouvernée, l’Institut national géographique (IGN) a organisé, hier mercredi 8 juillet à Cotonou, une Journée de validation de trois documents stratégiques. Il s’agit du Plan stratégique quinquennal 2015-2019, du Plan de formation triennal 2015-2017 et du rapport d’audit des installations photovoltaïques des stations permanentes CORS- GNSS du Bénin.
Dans son mot d’ouverture, le ministre en charge de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de l’Assainissement, Noël Fonton a rappelé l’importance des différents documents à valider au cours des assises. «A travers un plan stratégique assorti d’échéances et de moyens, une procédure formalisée de prise de décisions devra, désormais, dès validation, orienter et ce jusqu’en 2019, les différentes actions de l’Institut», indique le ministre. Pour lui, on ne saurait atteindre des résultats dans une entreprise sans des ressources humaines qualifiées.Il reste convaincu que le Plan de formation de l’IGN sur la période 2015-1017, lui permettra d’améliorer ses performances et de mieux servir les populations.
Parlant du troisième document relatif à l’audit des installations photovoltaïques des stations permanentes du Bénin, le ministre a rappelé qu’elles sont des héritages du Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) et dont leur gestion est confiée à l’IGN. «Ces installations méritent notre attention car constituant le réseau d’appui qui rassure la fiabilité des données pour une gestion saine et sécurisée du foncier et au-delà, pour un développement harmonieux de l’aménagement des territoires», souligne le ministre. Noël Fonton précise que l’un des défis importants du fonctionnement continu de ces stations permanentes est celui énergétique. L'audit permettra de repenser le dispositif des installations photovoltaïques en place aujourd’hui.
Le ministre a souhaité qu’au terme des travaux, les performances de l’IGN s’améliorent et qu’il dispose d’outils stratégiques de gestion de la plus grande importance.
Quant au directeur général de l’IGN, Roch Abdon Bah, il a exprimé à l’autorité les reconnaissances de tout le personnel pour son leadership. Puis il est revenu sur l’importance des différents documents à valider pour sa structure. «Sans tout cela, ce ne sera que du pilotage à vue. Ce que l’IGN ne saurait faire.», a-t-il conclu.
a4507.en:
La Nation Bénin...

For well-equipped management of its administration, the National Geographic Institute (IGN) organised yesterday, Wednesday 8 July, in Cotonou, a day for validating three strategic documents. The Minister responsible for Urban Planning, Housing and Sanitation, Noël Fonton, opened the proceedings.

In line with the logic of well-governed corporate management, the National Geographic Institute (IGN) organised, yesterday Wednesday 8 July in Cotonou, a day for validating three strategic documents. These are the Five-Year Strategic Plan 2015-2019, the Three-Year Training Plan 2015-2017 and the audit report on the photovoltaic installations of Benin's CORS-GNSS permanent stations.

In his opening remarks, the Minister responsible for Urban Planning, Housing and Sanitation, Noël Fonton, recalled the importance of the various documents to be validated during the session. "Through a strategic plan with deadlines and resources, a formalised decision-making procedure must, from now on and once validated, guide the Institute's various actions up to 2019," the minister stated. For him, results cannot be achieved in an organisation without qualified human resources. He remains convinced that IGN's training plan for the period 2015-2017 will allow it to improve its performance and better serve the population.

Speaking of the third document, relating to the audit of the photovoltaic installations of Benin's permanent stations, the minister recalled that they are a legacy of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) and that their management is entrusted to IGN. "These installations deserve our attention because they constitute the support network that ensures the reliability of data for sound and secure land management and, beyond that, for harmonious development of territorial planning," the minister stressed. Noël Fonton specifies that one of the important challenges of the continued operation of these permanent stations is energy. The audit will make it possible to rethink the photovoltaic installation arrangements in place today.

The minister expressed the wish that, at the end of the proceedings, IGN's performance would improve and that it would have strategic management tools of the greatest importance.

As for the director general of IGN, Roch Abdon Bah, he expressed to the authority the gratitude of all the staff for his leadership. He then returned to the importance of the various documents to be validated for his organisation. "Without all this, it would just be flying blind. That is something IGN could not do," he concluded.

a4640.t:
The United States government has announced a $450,000 grant to support emergency relief efforts in response to Tropical Cyclone Chido, which devastated parts of Mozambique in December last year.
Tropical Cyclone Chido brought heavy rainfall and strong winds, resulting in loss of life, injuries and significant destruction of homes and infrastructure in southern Cabo Delgado province and surrounding areas.
US ambassador Peter H. Vrooman emphasized the importance of swift action to help those affected by Cyclone Chido.
“The US government recognizes the immense challenges faced by the affected people and wants to reaffirm our solidarity. Our assistance will provide life-saving aid to those most impacted by the cyclone, helping to reduce human suffering and support recovery efforts,” Vrooman said.
Provided through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the funding is expected to address the urgent needs of affected populations across Cabo Delgado province, focusing on shelter, water, sanitation and hygiene assistance.
The Adventist Development and Relief Agency will implement one grant, while CARE International will undertake other rapid response work.
Additionally, other USAID humanitarian partners have chipped in with existing resources to help respond to immediate needs.
Assessments of the full scope of the disaster are ongoing and the US government is working closely with the National Institute for Disaster Management to coordinate the cyclone response.
JN/APA

MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – In a sharp pivot on U.S. military priorities, President Donald Trump on Tuesday told top military leaders that it is not the role of American forces to police distant countries such as Somalia and Kenya, warning instead of a growing threat “from within.”
The remarks come amid rising concerns that Washington may be preparing to scale back its counterterrorism operations in East Africa.
“Only in recent decades did politicians somehow come to believe that our job is to police the far reaches of Kenya and Somalia, while America is under invasion from within,” Trump said.
“We’re under invasion from within,” he repeated. “No different than a foreign enemy, but more difficult in many ways because they don’t wear uniforms. At least when they’re wearing a uniform you can take them out,” he added.
The remarks come as Trump continues to advocate for the deployment of US military forces in major American cities. He has referred to violent elements in urban areas as “domestic terrorists” and has pledged to take strong action to curb rising crime and homicide rates across the country.
The United States maintains a military presence in Somalia, where hundreds of troops support the Somali government in its fight against the militant group Al-Shabaab. American forces are involved in training Somali troops, providing combat advice, and conducting drone operations against insurgents.
Trump’s latest comments follow ongoing speculation over his administration’s long-term commitment to military operations in the Horn of Africa. During the final months of his presidency in 2020, he ordered the withdrawal of all US troops from Somalia.
Somali authorities have consistently expressed concerns that a reduced US military presence could jeopardize security in the country and embolden Al-Shabaab. The Islamist group has continued to launch deadly insurgency campaigns despite international efforts to degrade its capabilities.
In addition to US airstrikes and ground support, Somali forces have also received backing from clan militias and foreign partners, including the United Arab Emirates and Turkey. However, analysts warn that without sustained US support, Somalia’s fragile security gains could quickly unravel.

a4706.t:
Muktasari:
- Misaada hiyo mingi ikiwa kwenye sekta ya afya imesitishwa kufuatia agizo la Rais wa Marekani, Donald Trump, kusitisha shughuli za USAID.
Dar es Salaam. Nchi 132 ambazo zilikuwa zikinufaika moja kwa moja na ufadhili kutoka kwa Shirika la Misaada la Marekani (USAID), ziko hatarini kupoteza jumla ya watu 14 milioni kufikia mwaka 2030 baada ya kufungwa rasmi kwa shirika hilo la kutoa misaada.
Utafiti mpya uliochapishwa katika jarida la sayansi la Lancet unaeleza kwa kina jinsi hatua zilizopigwa katika miongo miwili iliyopita kupunguza vifo vya watoto na watu wazima, zinavyoweza kuporomoka kufutia hatua hiyo.
“Makadirio yetu yanaonyesha kuwa, kama hatua za kupunguza ufadhili zilizotangazwa na kutekelezwa katika nusu ya kwanza ya mwaka 2025 hazitaondolewa, idadi kubwa ya vifo vinavyoweza kuepukika vinaweza kutokea kufikia mwaka 2030,” wamesema watafiti.
Tofauti na kazi za utafiti za awali ambazo zilijikita tu kwenye athari za moja kwa moja za kiafya, utafiti huu mpya umeangazia pia athari mbadala ambazo pia zinaweza kusababisha vifo na kupoteza njia za kujikimu, na kueleza kuwa pia zinaathiri afya ya watu.
Mipango isiyo ya afya iliyofadhiliwa ni pamoja na misaada ya kifedha, kupunguza umaskini, elimu, na miradi ya maji na usafi wa mazingira.
“Makadirio yetu mara nyingi huwa juu zaidi kwa sababu yanazingatia si tu athari za moja kwa moja za miradi ya afya ya USAID kama tafiti za awali, bali pia athari pana za misaada ya USAID. Athari hizi zinaweza kuwa zimechangia sana katika mafanikio ya shirika hili kupunguza vifo,” wameeleza.
Wanasayansi hao wamesema kati ya mwaka 2000 na 2023, vifo vya watoto walio chini ya miaka mitano vilipungua kutoka 10.1 milioni hadi 4.8 milioni.
Hata hivyo, wanaonya kuwa hatua ya kusitisha msaada wa USAID inaweza kuvuruga mafanikio hayo na kufanya iwe vigumu kufikia Lengo la Maendeleo Endelevu la kupunguza vifo vya watoto hadi chini ya 25 kwa kila watoto 1,000 ifikapo 2030.
Uamuzi wa kufunga USAID ulitangazwa na Waziri wa Masuala ya Nje wa Marekani, Marco Rubio, kupitia hotuba ya maneno 900 iliyopewa jina “Make Foreign Aid Great Again”.
Raia wa Marekani hawapaswi kuendelea kulipa ushuru kusaidia serikali zisizofanya kazi katika mataifa ya mbali.
Utafiti unaonyesha kuwa kati ya 2001 hadi 2021, msaada wa USAID ulisaidia kupunguza malaria na magonjwa yaliyopuuzwa kwa zaidi ya asilimia 50 duniani.
Takwimu zinaonyesha kuwa ufadhili wa USAID ulipunguza vifo vya watoto kwa asilimia 44 na vifo vya watu wote kwa wastani wa asilimia 15.
Jumla ya vifo milioni 91 viliepushwa, ikiwa ni pamoja na vifo milioni 30 vya watoto wa umri wa chini ya miaka mitano.
Watafiti wanatahadharisha kuwa athari ya kukatiza msaada huo ni sawa na janga la kimataifa au vita vikuu, tofauti yake wanasema janga hili linaweza kuzuiliwa kwa mabadiliko ya kisera.
a4706.en:
14 million people at risk of dying, the cause being the suspension of USAID aid

Summary:
- Much of that aid, being in the health sector, has been halted following the order of the President of the United States, Donald Trump, to suspend the operations of USAID.

Dar es Salaam. The 132 countries that were benefiting directly from funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) are at risk of losing a total of 14 million people by the year 2030 after the formal closure of that aid agency.

A new study published in the science journal The Lancet explains in detail how the steps taken over the past two decades to reduce the deaths of children and adults could collapse as a result of that move.

"Our estimates show that, if the funding-cut measures announced and implemented in the first half of 2025 are not reversed, a large number of avoidable deaths could occur by 2030," the researchers said.

Unlike earlier research work, which focused only on the direct health effects, this new study has also examined the indirect effects, which can likewise cause deaths and the loss of livelihoods, explaining that these too affect people's health.

The non-health programmes that were funded include cash assistance, poverty reduction, education, and water and sanitation projects.

"Our estimates are often higher because they take into account not only the direct effects of USAID's health projects, as earlier studies did, but also the broader effects of USAID aid. These effects may have contributed greatly to this agency's success in reducing deaths," they explained.

Those scientists said that between the years 2000 and 2023, deaths of children under the age of five fell from 10.1 million to 4.8 million.

However, they warn that the move to halt USAID assistance could disrupt those gains and make it difficult to reach the Sustainable Development Goal of reducing child deaths to below 25 for every 1,000 children by 2030.

The decision to close USAID was announced by the United States Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, through a 900-word speech given the title "Make Foreign Aid Great Again".

American citizens should not continue to pay taxes to support governments that do not function in faraway nations.

Research shows that between 2001 and 2021, USAID assistance helped to reduce malaria and neglected diseases by more than 50 percent worldwide.

The figures show that USAID funding reduced child deaths by 44 percent and deaths of all people by an average of 15 percent.

A total of 91 million deaths were averted, including 30 million deaths of children under the age of five.

Researchers caution that the effect of cutting off that aid is equivalent to a global pandemic or a major war, the difference, they say, being that this catastrophe can be prevented through a change of policy.

a4831.t:
Le Maroc a défendu avec succès une trêve humanitaire pour le Ramadan au Soudan tout en plaidant pour l’intégrité territoriale de la RDC, au Conseil de paix et de sécurité de l’Union africaine.
Le Maroc a appelé à des résolutions pacifiques aux conflits au Soudan et en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) lors d’une réunion de haut niveau du Conseil de paix et de sécurité de l’Union africaine (CPS de l’UA), tenue vendredi à Addis-Abeba.
Nasser Bourita, ministre marocain des Affaires étrangères, qui dirigeait la délégation du pays en tant que membre du CPS de l’UA, a souligné que les solutions militaires ne résoudraient pas la crise soudanaise.
Intervenant lors de la réunion des chefs d’Etat et de gouvernement, M. Bourita a affirmé la solidarité du Maroc avec le Soudan et sa disposition à apporter le soutien nécessaire pour surmonter la crise actuelle.
La délégation marocaine a proposé avec succès une trêve humanitaire durant le mois de Ramadan prochain pour permettre l’accès sans restriction de l’aide humanitaire au Soudan. Cette proposition a reçu le soutien unanime des chefs d’Etat et de gouvernement réunis.
Concernant la crise à l’est de la RDC, Bourita a fortement plaidé pour l’engagement du Maroc en faveur de la souveraineté et de l’intégrité territoriale de la RDC.
« La persistance de cette instabilité compromet la paix et la sécurité continentales, mettant en péril les efforts de développement et la coopération régionale, ce qui nous oblige tous à agir avec détermination et responsabilité pour initier une dynamique de règlement pacifique, durable et soutenable du conflit », a-t-il affirmé.
Le Maroc a également affirmé que le dialogue et la négociation sont importants en ce moment, exprimant sa ferme opposition à toute forme de séparatisme. Le pays nord-africain a appelé à une cessation immédiate des hostilités, au respect du cessez-le-feu et à la reprise des négociations en RDC.
Bourita a également insisté sur la nécessité de remédier aux souffrances des civils en facilitant l’accès humanitaire aux populations affectées. « L’aide humanitaire doit être acheminée sans obstacles, en garantissant la protection des populations », a-t-il déclaré, appelant à des efforts coordonnés de la part de la communauté internationale et des acteurs régionaux.
La réunion a eu lieu, juste avant le sommet ordinaire des chefs d’État et de gouvernement de l’UA, prévu les 15 et 16 février.
La participation active du Maroc à ces discussions s’inscrit dans le cadre de sa position renforcée au sein de l’UA depuis son retour au sein de l’organisation en 2017 après 33 ans d’absence.
MK/te/Sf/APA
a4831.en:
Morocco successfully defended a humanitarian truce for Ramadan in Sudan while pleading for the territorial integrity of the DRC, at the Peace and Security Council of the African Union.

Morocco called for peaceful resolutions to the conflicts in Sudan and in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) at a high-level meeting of the African Union Peace and Security Council (AU PSC), held on Friday in Addis Ababa.

Nasser Bourita, Morocco's Minister of Foreign Affairs, who led the country's delegation as a member of the AU PSC, stressed that military solutions would not resolve the Sudanese crisis.

Speaking at the meeting of heads of state and government, Mr Bourita affirmed Morocco's solidarity with Sudan and its readiness to provide the necessary support to overcome the current crisis.

The Moroccan delegation successfully proposed a humanitarian truce during the coming month of Ramadan to allow unrestricted access for humanitarian aid to Sudan. This proposal received the unanimous support of the assembled heads of state and government.

Concerning the crisis in the east of the DRC, Bourita strongly pleaded for Morocco's commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC.

"The persistence of this instability compromises continental peace and security, jeopardising development efforts and regional cooperation, which obliges us all to act with determination and responsibility in order to initiate a dynamic of a peaceful, lasting and sustainable settlement of the conflict," he affirmed.

Morocco also affirmed that dialogue and negotiation are important at this moment, expressing its firm opposition to any form of separatism. The North African country called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, respect for the ceasefire and the resumption of negotiations in the DRC.

Bourita also insisted on the need to remedy the suffering of civilians by facilitating humanitarian access to the affected populations. "Humanitarian aid must be delivered without obstacles, guaranteeing the protection of the populations," he declared, calling for coordinated efforts from the international community and regional actors.

The meeting took place just before the ordinary summit of AU heads of state and government, scheduled for 15 and 16 February.

Morocco's active participation in these discussions is part of its strengthened position within the AU since its return to the organisation in 2017 after 33 years of absence.

a5038.t:
Herbert von Karajan once gave the Berlin Philharmonic a sound the world could recognise in a single phrase. That is the challenge before Muhammad Ali Pate. He has built architecture where there was none, compelled governors and partners into one compact, channelled billions directly to frontline clinics, expanded insurance, revitalised immunisation, embedded nutrition into health planning, commissioned oncology centres, rehabilitated teaching hospitals, shaped policies to stem the exodus of health workers and dared to enforce tempo.
In April 1955, the Berlin Philharmonic faced a moment of uncertainty. Its great conductor, Wilhelm Furtwängler, had died, leaving behind one of the world’s finest orchestras but no one to hold it together. A hall of virtuosos risked splintering into noise. Then Herbert von Karajan stepped to the podium. With a single lift of his baton, the fragments became a symphony. Over the next three decades, he shaped the Philharmonic’s identity so profoundly that critics said he did not merely conduct, he disciplined chaos into harmony.
A philharmonic, from the Greek for “love of harmony,” is never just an assembly of players. It is a fragile balance of strings, brass, woodwinds and percussion — each capable of brilliance, yet each able to overwhelm the others. The conductor does not play a note but interprets the score, sets the tempo, and ensures that every part breathes together. Without that hand, there is cacophony. With it, there is music.
Nigeria’s health system has long resembled an orchestra without such a conductor. Ministries, thirty-six states, development partners, local councils and overstretched health workers all played their parts, but too often in fragmented isolation. The result was duplication, waste and silence in moments when lives depended on sound. It was into this hall that Muhammad Ali Pate returned in August 2023, leaving a senior position at the World Bank, a Harvard professorship, and a global role at Gavi. He came home not as a soloist seeking applause but as a conductor determined to draw coherence from a fractured score.
The instrument he chose was the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative (NHSRII). Within four months, at the behest of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Pate brought every governor and seventeen development partners into one Compact at the Presidential Villa. At the core lay a Sector-Wide approach (SWAp) hinged on one plan, one budget, one report and one conversation, which for the first time placed Nigeria’s health system under a unified framework for alignment, resource convergence and accountability – on a path to amplifying impact on population health outcomes. A SWAp Programme Management Unit was established within the Presidency itself, giving the reform endeavour a podium at the highest political level. Anchored on the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda, health reform gained political cover and urgency. Billions of dollars in commitments were aligned to a single score.
Primary health centres are the strings of Nigeria’s orchestra, carrying the melody and shaping the rhythm of daily health. Here the most visible transformation has begun. Nearly ₦90 billion has been disbursed directly to more than eight thousand primary healthcare facilities, money once lost in bureaucracy now reaching the nurses and midwives in charge in the facilities. Over a thousand, three hundred centres have already been fully revitalised, with more than five thousand more underway, towards a target of seventeen thousand functional PHCs across the country. Power, water, cold chain equipment and diagnostics are starting to replace the emptiness of painted walls. In just the first quarter of 2025, more than thirty-seven million Nigerians sought care at this level – from 10 million in the same quarter in 2024, signalling improved confidence in the health system.
To sustain this rhythm, the new Community-Based Procurement Platform was launched under the ₦17 billion Social Action Fund. It geo-tags procurement to the ward level, empowers local organisations, and assigns compliance officers across all seven hundred and seventy-four local government areas. Women-led and disability-focused community organisations are no longer left out — they are now embedded in procurement governance.
But melody alone does not fill a hall. The brass must add force. Pate’s answer has been the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain. He has long argued that no nation is secure if it imports the medicines on which its survival depends. By 2025, the initiative had attracted more than $5 billion in bankable projects, including $1 billion each from Afrexim Bank and the European Investment Bank, and more than $200 million from a single manufacturer.
Equity became the principle behind the score. Clinics are being upgraded across all the states – with no community left behind. Insurance coverage, once a distant dream of the poor, expanded from sixteen million people in 2023 to twenty million by early 2025. Premium subsidies now protect vulnerable households from the financial shocks of illness. The Catastrophic Health Insurance Fund, approved in the 2025 budget, is targeting high-cost conditions such as cancer and kidney disease — conditions that often drive families into poverty.
Three new oncology centres have opened in Katsina, Enugu and Benin, with three more in the pipeline. State performance scorecards and strict enforcement of a SWAp incentive framework are compelling governors to align to the NHSRII priorities (through revamped State annual operating plans) and match commitment with cash or in kind contributions, such as in human resource, facility revisitation, digital health infrastructure and the supply of essential commodities. Nigeria now leads the continent in governance, resource convergence and accountability under the SWAp compact. While out-of-pocket spending still exceeds seventy per cent, the foundations for fairer more equitable financing are finally being laid.
Maternal and child health is no longer an afterthought. Through the NHIA-empanelled MAMII, one hundred and seventy-two local government areas — home to half of all maternal deaths — are now prioritised. Since 2023, more than thirteen million antenatal visits and four million skilled deliveries have been recorded, alongside thousands of free caesarean sections. Fourteen million adolescent girls have received HPV vaccines, and fifty thousand previously unreached children were covered in one hundred focus local government areas. Prevention is finding its place beside cure.
But melody alone does not fill a hall. The brass must add force. Pate’s answer has been the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain. He has long argued that no nation is secure if it imports the medicines on which its survival depends. By 2025, the initiative had attracted more than $5 billion in bankable projects, including $1 billion each from Afrexim Bank and the European Investment Bank, and more than $200 million from a single manufacturer. Six international firms have announced plans to begin production in Nigeria, supported by an Executive Order waiving import duties on machinery and raw materials. Alongside this industrial drive, federal teaching hospitals have begun long overdue rehabilitation – part of a strategy to restore them as centres of excellence and reduce dependence on medical tourism. It was the brass section entering with force and confidence.
Even so, percussion intruded. Cholera flared with the rains and diphtheria struck again, outbreaks beating their drums across communities. The Ministry responded by creating the Nigeria Preparedness and Readiness Alert System, a predictive platform, and by training more than three hundred infection prevention officers across hospitals. These were important beats, but percussion cannot dominate. Without safe water, sanitation and resilient vaccination, outbreaks will continue to cut into the melody.
No orchestra can survive without breath. In music it comes from the woodwinds. In health it comes from the workforce. Nigeria’s doctors, nurses and midwives provide this balance, but their sound is thinning. Of one hundred and thirty thousand doctors ever registered, fewer than sixty thousand remained active in 2023, and every month more leave for the United Kingdom, Canada or the Gulf. To respond, a Health Workforce Migration Policy has been introduced — the first structured framework to manage this exodus by balancing mobility with national needs and by negotiating fairer terms with destination countries. Alongside it, the National Health Fellows Programme has placed young professionals in every local government area, offering presence and accountability at the primary level. Together they are early steps to keep the orchestra breathing rather than gasping for air.
Reforms to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund are underway. Discussions are ongoing to deduct counterpart funding at source, raise the CRF share above one per cent, and earmark part of FAAC savings for health, school feeding and social protection. These actions would stabilise the base for vaccine access, health security, health insurance, local manufacturing and primary care.
Then, in a defining act, President Tinubu, early this month, on advice from the Health Ministry, issued a directive that no procurement, licence, or regulatory approval would proceed without the proof of health insurance. The NHIA certificate is now as essential as a tax ID. Health financing finally has a tempo, and enforcement is the new baton. The target is clear: forty-four million Nigerians insured by 2030, forming the largest risk pool on the continent. Fiscal conditions now permit it. The national deficit has dropped from 5.4 to 3 per cent of GDP. Revenues have risen to 11.5 per cent. Thirty-four states are reporting surpluses. It is finally possible to fund dignity.
New energy is coming from the diaspora. Several now enable structured remittances that fund health insurance for families back home. Health taxes on tobacco, alcohol and sugar-sweetened beverages are under review—not just for their deterrent effect, but to unlock new fiscal space and make Nigerians healthier.
Reforms to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund are underway. Discussions are ongoing to deduct counterpart funding at source, raise the CRF share above one per cent, and earmark part of FAAC savings for health, school feeding and social protection. These actions would stabilise the base for vaccine access, health security, health insurance, local manufacturing and primary care.
The true measure will not be found in compacts or memoranda. It will be in lives. Success is a midwife in Zamfara who can count on oxytocin and a working lamp at two in the morning. It is an officer in Rivers who can resolve a stockout in hours rather than days. It is a carpenter in Onitsha who can refill his hypertension drugs predictably every month without selling a goat. Failure is subtler — a clinic with new paint but empty fridges, a governor who signs a compact but withholds counterpart funds, an insurance card that buys nothing.
Herbert von Karajan once gave the Berlin Philharmonic a sound the world could recognise in a single phrase. That is the challenge before Muhammad Ali Pate. He has built architecture where there was none, compelled governors and partners into one compact, channelled billions directly to frontline clinics, expanded insurance, revitalised immunisation, embedded nutrition into health planning, commissioned oncology centres, rehabilitated teaching hospitals, shaped policies to stem the exodus of health workers and dared to enforce tempo. And he has done so under the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu, whose political cover has given reform legitimacy and urgency.
The orchestra is vast, the score ambitious, the stakes life and death. Whether Nigeria finally hears the music of renewal will depend on whether the conductor can hold the tempo long enough for harmony to emerge. Then, Nigeria may at last hear its long delayed symphony of health.
Chinedu Moghalu is the senior special adviser on Strategic Communication, Stakeholder Engagement and Advocacy to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, while Muntaqa Umar Sadiq is the National Coordinator of the Sector-wide Coordinating Office-Programme Management Unit.

Guantanamo Bay inmate Ridah Bin Saleh al-Yazidi has been repatriated to Tunisia, the United States (US) Department of Defence has said.
He was found eligible for transfer from the detention facility after a “rigorous interagency review process”, a press statement said.
The Pentagon did not say if Yazidi had accepted any guilt.
Since 2002, the Guantanamo Bay detention facility has been used to hold what the US describes as captured unlawful combatants during America’s “war on terror”.
The camp is part of a US naval base complex in south-eastern Cuba.
- Advertisement -
According to an unconfirmed report by the New York Times, Yazidi was never charged and was approved for transfer more than a decade ago.
The newspaper also said he had been at Guantanamo Bay since the facility was first set up in 2002.
According to Monday’s Pentagon statement, 26 detainees remain at Guantanamo Bay, of whom 14 are eligible for transfer.
Earlier in December, the Pentagon announced that the US had repatriated three other detainees, the Associated Press news agency reported.

The camp was established by the George Bush administration to detain the most dangerous suspects for interrogation and the prosecution of war crimes.
Controversy has centred around the period of time detainees have been held without charge and the use of interrogation techniques.—BBC

a5164.t:
Que pensent les pays africains de la victoire de Donald Trump aux USA? Alors que la plupart des pays occidentaux préféraient nettement une victoire du camp démocrate, on a quelques informations sur les réactions de plusieurs pays africains.
Le Burundi, pays très critiqué par les pays occidentaux et qui a annoncé il y’a quelque temps son retrait de la cour pénale internationale, a été le premier pays africain à féliciter Donald Trump pour son élection.
La RDC également très critiquée, a rajouté espérer que le nouveau président ne s’ingère pas dans la politique intérieure des pays africains.
Toutefois, la président Ellen Johnson Sirleaf du Libéria, pays très lié aux USA de par son histoire, s’est dite inquiète appelant le président Trump à ne pas remettre en cause les différents rapports entre les USA et l’Afrique.
Le Burkina Faso, qui a tourné la page de décennie de dictature déguisée, a de son côté affirmé que le nouveau président élu devra composer avec la communauté internationale.
a5164.en:
Donald Trump’s victory: Burundi and the DRC rejoice

What do African countries think of Donald Trump’s victory in the USA? While most Western countries clearly preferred a victory for the Democratic camp, we have some information on the reactions of several African countries.

Burundi, a country heavily criticised by Western countries and which announced some time ago its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court, was the first African country to congratulate Donald Trump on his election.

The DRC, also heavily criticised, added that it hopes the new president will not interfere in the internal politics of African countries.

However, President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf of Liberia, a country very closely linked to the USA by its history, said she was worried, calling on President Trump not to call into question the various relations between the USA and Africa.

Burkina Faso, which has turned the page on a decade of disguised dictatorship, for its part stated that the new president-elect will have to work with the international community.
